question: What is another common name for the limbic system?
explanation: The limbic system is widely known as the emotional brain because it regulates moods, feelings, and basic survival instincts. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h1)

question: Where is the limbic system located in the brain?

options.A: Inside the hollow cavities of the cerebellum
options.B: At the very front tip of the frontal lobes
options.C: On the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.D: Deep inside the brain surrounding the brainstem

explanation: Spot on! The structures making up the limbic system sit deep inside, wrapping around the top of the brainstem right beneath the outer cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h1)

question: Which part of the limbic system looks like a seahorse and helps with memory?
explanation: You got it! The hippocampus has a distinct seahorse shape and is essential for helping you form and process new memories. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the amygdala within the limbic system?

options.D: Filtering visual images from the eyes

explanation: The almond-shaped amygdala plays a central role in detecting danger in the environment and generating emotional reactions like fear. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why does the amygdala let you react to danger before you even have time to think?

options.A: Danger signals reach the amygdala super fast before slow conscious thought kicks in
options.B: Rational thought happens only inside the spinal cord
options.C: The cerebral cortex controls all immediate physical reflexes
options.D: The amygdala temporarily shuts down the eyes to focus on hearing

explanation: Exactly! Messages from your senses take a fast track to the amygdala so you can react quickly to danger before your thinking brain even catches up. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h3)

question: Which emotion is most directly tied to the quick action of the amygdala?
explanation: Spot on! Fear and quick threat detection are primary functions driven by the amygdala to help keep your body safe from harm. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h3)

question: What happens when a person suffers severe damage to their hippocampus?

options.A: They lose the ability to feel physical pain
options.B: They experience paralysis in their lower limbs
options.C: They forget all their childhood memories
options.D: They can no longer form new long-term memories

explanation: You nailed it! The hippocampus is needed to lock in new experiences into long-term storage, so damage makes forming new memories very difficult. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h4)

question: How does the hippocampus work when it comes to human memory?

options.A: It acts as the final permanent storage vault for every memory
options.B: It translates what you see into spoken words
options.C: It organizes new memories and helps send them to the cortex
options.D: It deletes sad memories to protect your mental health

explanation: Correct! Think of the hippocampus as a sorting station that processes new memories and helps ship them to the cerebral cortex for permanent storage. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is the main job of the hypothalamus when you experience stress?

options.A: Slowing down your heart rate so you can fall asleep
options.B: Filtering visual signals coming from your eyes
options.C: Linking emotional triggers to physical stress and hormone responses
options.D: Storing facts you learned during your nursing lectures

explanation: You got it! The hypothalamus connects emotional feelings from the limbic system to physical body changes by triggering hormones and your nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which physical reaction does the hypothalamus trigger during a fight-or-flight response?
explanation: Spot on! Stress hormones released via the hypothalamus make your heart beat faster to pump extra oxygen and blood to your muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h5)

question: A patient with post-traumatic stress disorder startles violently at a sudden loud noise. Which limbic structure is most likely driving this hyperactive reaction?
explanation: An overactive amygdala is responsible for the exaggerated fear and startle responses seen in conditions like PTSD. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h6)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT linked to problems in the limbic system?
explanation: Correct! Iron deficiency anemia is a blood and nutrition issue, whereas anxiety, depression, and PTSD are all tied to limbic system imbalances. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h6)
